items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Rex and I became very good friends

ctx.x: When the sign for the last number would be held up and the band that would be playing the last number of the set hit the introduction of the number, the hoppers would come out jumping from every corner of the Savoy as if there was a stampede to see who could get to the middle of the dance floor first. I really got my kicks when it was time to play the last number of the set watching those cats come out jumping like broncos.

Rex and I became very good friends and we started going to bars and jam sessions together. A fellow from Chicago came to New York and opened a hangout for musicians called the Rhythm Club on 131st Street near 7th Avenue. There were pool tables and card games and like the bars, the club was open 24 hours a day. Bert Hall was the name of the owner. Musicians who were married and had sweethearts that wanted to get in touch with them could have their chicks call them on the phone or receive letters at the club. When…

The big attraction however would be jam sessions at least twice a week. A sign would be put up on the board announcing a supper for a certain date in order to let the word get around. Jam sessions were called suppers. Saxophone supper, trumpet supper etc. The musicians and occasionally a drummer banjo and bass. But the majority of the time there would only be some pianists.
